newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Andhra Pradesh assesses cyclone crop losses.
newsitem.headline: India's Andhra Pradesh assesses cyclone crop losses.

text.p: A cyclone which may have killed 2,000 people in India's Andhra Pradesh state caused losses to property and crops amounting to 53.75 billion rupees ($1.5 billion), the state's chief minister said on Monday.
Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu told a press conference that the greatest financial losses from the cyclone which struck last Wednesday were in coconut groves.
Naidu put a 30 billion rupee ($839 million) value on the lost trees, which take 15 years to reach full maturity.
Some five million trees were destroyed by the 180 kmph (110 mph) winds and tidal waves that ravaged this southeastern state's coastline.
Many villagers who depended on the coconut groves for their livelihood died after being crushed beneath the trunks of trees uprooted and hurled through their houses by the violent storm.

The storm destroyed rice paddy crops in the the Konaseema region known as the rice bowl of Andhra Pradesh over an area of 336,000 hectares (830,256 acres) and the loss was estimated at 3.36 billion rupees ($94 million), Naidu said.
The value of other crops destroyed -- bananas, sugar cane cashewnuts, palm oil and betelnut -- was around 14.28 billion rupees ($400 million).
Several thousand head of cattle and four million poultry birds also perished, he said.
